analysis.title: Market Intelligence: US Morning Update (22 October 2026)
key_insights: Asia equities fell sharply Thursday as Brent futures spiked and the AI trade grew more volatile in earnings season. Japan, Korea and Hong Kong each declined nearly 3%.
European equities are lower on energy cost concerns. Front-month Brent is up about $3 to about $112/bbl.
Across asset classes, growth concerns are outweighing inflation concerns after the oil spike. The US 10-year Treasury yield is 5bps lower at 5.07%.

Focus on AI infrastructure durability. The risks named are local opposition to data centers, a shortage of construction labor and critical components, and questions about whether fixed income investors will keep lending to data center developers.
GS bottom line: demand for compute capacity far outstrips supply, which implies a strong tailwind to AI infrastructure earnings growth.

CRWV (Borges): CoreWeave needs about $23bn of new debt to serve its backlog and bring online its secured 4.2GW of power, assuming a 4.5 year GPU useful life matching contract duration. The figure falls to $19.5bn if useful life extends to 6 years.

NVDA (Schneider): GTC Berlin keynote reinforced GS's view that AI deployments remain on track. Nvidia is taking steps to ensure supply chain preparedness and offering tools for safety and security concerns tied to agentic AI.

SPCX (Sheridan): the Super Intelligence division (the cloud provider) is producing upside from scaling compute at a compelling spend per GW versus industry averages, with strong monetization in Cloud Services given the supply/demand imbalance.

META (Sheridan, Buy): 3Q26 revenue beat, with core advertising growth of +26% YoY and 10mn+ advertisers using generative AI ad features. Muse, a consumer agentic platform, has about 10mm downloads in UCAN. Reality Labs losses are moderating. 12m price target raised to $885 from $860.

TSLA (Delaney, Neutral): broadly in-line 3Q earnings with the stock -4% pre-market. FSD is above 75% of new North America deliveries, cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles reached 3.1mn, and gross margin beat across all three segments. Higher opex and capex weigh on profitability and FCF, and competition caps the EPS ramp. Optimus progress was weaker. 12m price target $360.

US Pharma 3Q26 preview (Haider): expects beat or in-line results next week. Favors LLY and JNJ for growth and MRK for post patent cliff recovery. Focus on pipeline execution for PFE and BMY and commercial execution at ABBV.

NKE (Roach, Neutral): management meeting highlighted a $2.5bn PACE run-rate savings opportunity across SG&A and supply chain gross margin, continued China and Jordan resets, and a resource shift from Beaverton into local markets. Key to watch is the Investor Day and FY31 financial view. 12m price target $30.
Korea: the central bank held its policy rate and kept a hawkish stance. GS expects the next hike in 1Q27 but does not rule out November.
Germany: September federal spending came in below expectations, but not enough to change GS's expectation of notable fiscal expansion in 2026.
GS economists see tightening in European financial conditions across several indicators, which could substitute for some ECB policy tightening.
Rating changes: A.P. Moeller-Maersk cut to Sell from Neutral. Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders initiated at Sell.

Other earnings notes not on the call: LUV 3Q beat on stronger revenue with 4Q outlook midpoint below consensus on higher costs. UAL 3Q in line with better-than-expected 4Q revenue outlook. PM strong Q3 but FY26 guidance lowered on higher costs. TMO and DHR 3Q beats or derisked guides. TXN strong quarter and guidance. LRCX bullish 2027 WFE commentary against elevated expectations. T beat and raise but higher costs weigh on outlook. IBM solid quarter with Software upside.

earnings_insights: META 3Q26: revenue beat reported 10/21 after the close, with core advertising growth of +26% YoY. Reality Labs segment losses are moderating.
TSLA 3Q26: broadly in-line results reported 10/21 after the close, with a gross margin beat across all three segments. Stock -4% pre-market.
LUV 3Q: beat on stronger revenue, with the 4Q outlook midpoint below consensus on higher fuel and non-fuel costs.
UAL 3Q: in line, with the 4Q revenue outlook better than expected.
PM 3Q: strong results, with FY26 guidance lowered on higher costs.
IHG 3Q26: RevPAR growth of +5.3%, with management confident of FY26 EPS growth at the top of the 12-15% target range.
KNX 3Q26: EPS beat, with the 4Q guide range above consensus.
TMO 3Q26: beat and raise driven by the Lab Products and Services segment. DHR 3Q26: FY26 respiratory guide derisked.

TXN: strong quarter and guidance with solid gross margin leverage. LRCX: solid quarter with bullish 2027 WFE commentary. IBM: solid quarter with Software upside and Consulting inflection. T: beat and raise, but higher costs and working capital weigh on the outlook.
Reporting before the open 10/22: BX, CBRE, NDAQ, CMCSA, HBAN, DGX, DOW, HON, LMT, PHM, ROP, UNP, PGE, VLO, PG, TSCO and others.
